Two hundred denarii was therefore well over half a year’s wages."},{"verse":14,"phrase":"the Prophet","lemma":"προφήτης","kind":"background","traditional":"","note":"Many Jews expected a prophet like Moses, promised in Deuteronomy 18:15–18. A miraculous feeding in a remote place near Passover would have recalled Moses and the manna, which explains both this reaction and the attempt to make Jesus king in the next verse."},{"verse":19,"phrase":"twenty-five or thirty stadia","lemma":"στάδιον","kind":"background","traditional":"","note":"A stadion was about 185 meters, so the distance is roughly three to three and a half miles (five to six kilometers). That places the boat far out from shore."},{"verse":20,"phrase":"It is I","lemma":"εἰμί","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"It is I","note":"The Greek is literally “I am,” the ordinary way of saying “It’s me.” In the Greek Old Testament the same words also serve as God’s self-declaration, and John has Jesus use them that way elsewhere (8:58). Many scholars hear that overtone here, in a scene of mastery over the sea; others take it as simple self-identification."},{"verse":27,"phrase":"eternal life","lemma":"αἰώνιος","kind":"background","traditional":"eternal life, everlasting life","note":"In Jewish usage of the period, “eternal life” is the life of the age to come. The word describes a kind of life as well as its unending length. In John the believer already has this life (verse 47), though resurrection “on the last day” is still to come."},{"verse":31,"phrase":"He gave them bread from heaven to eat","lemma":"","kind":"background","traditional":"","note":"The quotation is closest to Psalm 78:24 and recalls the manna story of Exodus 16. The crowd is asking Jesus to match Moses. The grumbling in verses 41 and 61 uses the word the Greek Old Testament uses for Israel’s complaints in the wilderness."},{"verse":33,"phrase":"that which comes down from heaven","lemma":"καταβαίνω","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"he who comes down from heaven","note":"The Greek can mean either “that which comes down” (the bread) or “he who comes down” (a person), because “bread” is grammatically masculine. The crowd’s reply in verse 34 shows they heard it of bread; verse 35 reveals that Jesus means himself. Translations are divided, and the double meaning is probably intended."},{"verse":54,"phrase":"eats","lemma":"τρώγω","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"eats (some versions: feeds on)","note":"From here to verse 58 John switches to a different Greek verb for eating, one that in older Greek meant to gnaw or munch. Some interpreters see a deliberately more physical word and render it “feeds on” or “chews.” Many lexicographers hold that by this period it had become an everyday present-tense word for “eat,” so it is rendered “eats” here."},{"verse":60,"phrase":"harsh","lemma":"σκληρός","kind":"departure","traditional":"This is a hard saying","note":"“Hard” in modern English suggests “difficult to understand.” The Greek word means hard in the sense of harsh, rough or offensive. The disciples are complaining that the saying is intolerable, not that it is obscure."},{"verse":61,"phrase":"cause you to stumble","lemma":"σκανδαλίζω","kind":"departure","traditional":"Does this offend you?","note":"The verb means to trip someone up so that they fall in their loyalty to God. “Offend” now suggests hurt feelings, which is too weak for a saying that makes many disciples leave (verse 66). Modern versions are divided here between “offend” and “cause to stumble.”"},{"verse":63,"phrase":"The Spirit","lemma":"πνεῦμα","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"It is the Spirit who gives life","note":"Greek manuscripts did not distinguish capital letters, so “spirit” here could be God’s Spirit or spirit as opposed to flesh. Most translations capitalize the first occurrence and leave the second (“are spirit and are life”) in lowercase, as here, but the line between the two is not sharp in John."},{"verse":64,"phrase":"hand him over","lemma":"παραδίδωμι","kind":"departure","traditional":"betray him","note":"The Greek verb is the ordinary word for handing a person into someone else’s custody. The Gospels use the same word for what Judas, the chief priests and Pilate each do to Jesus. Most versions render it “betray” when Judas is the subject, which fits the context but hides that chain. Some scholars defend “betray” as a legitimate contextual sense."},{"verse":69,"phrase":"the Holy One of God","lemma":"ἅγιος","kind":"textual","traditional":"that Christ, the Son of the living God","note":"Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read “the Christ, the Son of the living God.” The earliest witnesses have the shorter “the Holy One of God.” The longer form is generally judged to have been adapted to Peter’s confession in Matthew 16:16."}],"candidates":[{"lemma":"μένω","rendering":"endure (v. 27) / remain (v. 56)","verse":27,"reason":"A key Johannine word that translators render variously as abide, remain, stay, dwell, endure or last, and readers lose the thread if it varies between chapters."},{"lemma":"σημεῖον","rendering":"sign","verse":2,"reason":"John’s term for Jesus’s mighty acts; versions vary between “sign” and “miracle,” and the Gospel’s argument depends on the word being recognizable throughout."},{"lemma":"τρώγω","rendering":"eat","verse":54,"reason":"Translators split between “eat,” “feed on” and “chew” here and in John 13:18 and Matthew 24:38, and the choice implies a view on whether the verb is emphatic."},{"lemma":"κύριος","rendering":"Sir (v. 34) / Lord (v. 68)","verse":34,"reason":"The vocative κύριε ranges from polite “Sir” to confessional “Lord,” and a consistent rule is needed for when each is used across the Gospels."},{"lemma":"πατήρ","rendering":"ancestors (plural, of Israel’s forebears)","verse":31,"reason":"The plural for Israel’s forebears is split between “fathers” and “ancestors” across versions and recurs throughout the Gospels, Acts, Paul and Hebrews."}]}

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this Jesus went away across the Sea of Galilee, the Sea of Tiberias.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A large crowd was following him, because they saw the signs he was performing on the sick.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus went up the mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the Passover, the festival of the Jews, was near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when Jesus looked up and saw that a large crowd was coming toward him, he said to Philip,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Where are we to buy bread so that these people may eat?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Bread worth two hundred denarii would not be enough for each of them to get a little.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish—but what are these among so many?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have the people sit down.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now there was plenty of grass in the place. So the men sat down, about five thousand in number.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus took the loaves, and after giving thanks he distributed them to those who were seated, and likewise of the fish, as much as they wanted.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they were satisfied, he said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Gather up the leftover pieces, so that nothing is lost.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with pieces from the five barley loaves, left over by those who had eaten.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the people saw the sign he had performed, they began to say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This truly is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus, knowing that they were about to come and seize him to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself, alone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: got into a boat, and set out across the sea for Capernaum. Darkness had already fallen, and Jesus had not yet come to them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and the sea was being stirred up because a strong wind was blowing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they wanted to take him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the land they were heading for.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The next day the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the sea saw that there had been no other small boat there except one, and that Jesus had not gotten into the boat with his disciples, but his disciples had gone away alone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But small boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the small boats and went to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they found him on the other side of the sea, they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbi, when did you get here?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, you are looking for me not because you saw signs but because you ate of the loaves and had your fill.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not work for the food that perishes but for the food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on him God the Father has set his seal.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What are we to do, so that we may work the works of God?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This is the work of God: that you believe in the one he sent.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Then what sign are you going to perform, so that we may see it and believe you? What work are you doing?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Our ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven; rather, my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For the bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, give us this bread always.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I told you that you have seen me and yet do not believe.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: All that the Father gives me will come to me, and the one who comes to me I will never throw out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: because I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And this is the will of the one who sent me: that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise it up on the last day.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this is the will of my Father: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews began grumbling about him because he had said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the bread that came down from heaven,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can he now say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Stop grumbling among yourselves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them, and I will raise them up on the last day.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is written in the Prophets, ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the bread of life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Your ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, they will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews began quarreling with one another, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For my flesh is true food, and my blood is true drink.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will also live because of me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: This is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like what the ancestors ate, and died; whoever eats this bread will live forever.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said these things in the synagogue as he was teaching in Capernaum.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this, many of his disciples said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This saying is harsh; who can listen to it?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples were grumbling about this, said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Does this cause you to stumble?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then what if you see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The Spirit is the one who gives life; the flesh is of no use at all. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But there are some of you who do not believe.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For Jesus knew from the beginning who those were who did not believe, and who it was that would hand him over.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been granted to them by the Father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At this, many of his disciples turned back and no longer went about with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to the Twelve,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not want to go away too, do you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon Peter answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and we have come to believe and to know that you are the Holy One of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Did I not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was speaking of Judas son of Simon Iscariot, for this man, one of the Twelve, was going to hand him over.

notes.note: A denarius was a Roman silver coin, roughly a day’s pay for a laborer. Two hundred denarii was therefore well over half a year’s wages.

Many Jews expected a prophet like Moses, promised in Deuteronomy 18:15–18. A miraculous feeding in a remote place near Passover would have recalled Moses and the manna, which explains both this reaction and the attempt to make Jesus king in the next verse.
A stadion was about 185 meters, so the distance is roughly three to three and a half miles (five to six kilometers). That places the boat far out from shore.

The Greek is literally “I am,” the ordinary way of saying “It’s me.” In the Greek Old Testament the same words also serve as God’s self-declaration, and John has Jesus use them that way elsewhere (8:58). Many scholars hear that overtone here, in a scene of mastery over the sea; others take it as simple self-identification.

In Jewish usage of the period, “eternal life” is the life of the age to come. The word describes a kind of life as well as its unending length. In John the believer already has this life (verse 47), though resurrection “on the last day” is still to come.

notes.phrase: He gave them bread from heaven to eat
notes.note: The quotation is closest to Psalm 78:24 and recalls the manna story of Exodus 16. The crowd is asking Jesus to match Moses. The grumbling in verses 41 and 61 uses the word the Greek Old Testament uses for Israel’s complaints in the wilderness.

notes.phrase: that which comes down from heaven
notes.traditional: he who comes down from heaven
notes.note: The Greek can mean either “that which comes down” (the bread) or “he who comes down” (a person), because “bread” is grammatically masculine. The crowd’s reply in verse 34 shows they heard it of bread; verse 35 reveals that Jesus means himself. Translations are divided, and the double meaning is probably intended.

From here to verse 58 John switches to a different Greek verb for eating, one that in older Greek meant to gnaw or munch. Some interpreters see a deliberately more physical word and render it “feeds on” or “chews.” Many lexicographers hold that by this period it had become an everyday present-tense word for “eat,” so it is rendered “eats” here.

“Hard” in modern English suggests “difficult to understand.” The Greek word means hard in the sense of harsh, rough or offensive. The disciples are complaining that the saying is intolerable, not that it is obscure.

The verb means to trip someone up so that they fall in their loyalty to God. “Offend” now suggests hurt feelings, which is too weak for a saying that makes many disciples leave (verse 66). Modern versions are divided here between “offend” and “cause to stumble.”

notes.traditional: It is the Spirit who gives life
notes.note: Greek manuscripts did not distinguish capital letters, so “spirit” here could be God’s Spirit or spirit as opposed to flesh. Most translations capitalize the first occurrence and leave the second (“are spirit and are life”) in lowercase, as here, but the line between the two is not sharp in John.

The Greek verb is the ordinary word for handing a person into someone else’s custody. The Gospels use the same word for what Judas, the chief priests and Pilate each do to Jesus. Most versions render it “betray” when Judas is the subject, which fits the context but hides that chain. Some scholars defend “betray” as a legitimate contextual sense.

notes.traditional: that Christ, the Son of the living God
notes.note: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read “the Christ, the Son of the living God.” The earliest witnesses have the shorter “the Holy One of God.” The longer form is generally judged to have been adapted to Peter’s confession in Matthew 16:16.

candidates.reason: A key Johannine word that translators render variously as abide, remain, stay, dwell, endure or last, and readers lose the thread if it varies between chapters.
John’s term for Jesus’s mighty acts; versions vary between “sign” and “miracle,” and the Gospel’s argument depends on the word being recognizable throughout.
Translators split between “eat,” “feed on” and “chew” here and in John 13:18 and Matthew 24:38, and the choice implies a view on whether the verb is emphatic.
The vocative κύριε ranges from polite “Sir” to confessional “Lord,” and a consistent rule is needed for when each is used across the Gospels.
The plural for Israel’s forebears is split between “fathers” and “ancestors” across versions and recurs throughout the Gospels, Acts, Paul and Hebrews.
